title: A Japanese paragraph pairing a Latin ascii face with an MS Gothic / MS Mincho / MS PGothic eastAsia face paces every line at the East Asian factor whatever the Latin partner; gen leads the strut and the spans with the runs' own East Asian metric face
source: probes /tmp/msgothic-probe/explicit-plain.docx + explicit2.docx -> Word for Mac direct PDF (2026-11-07), pymupdf rawdict baselines, A4, docDefaults Calibri 11 + useFELayout, 4-line paragraphs alternating kana-only and kana + Latin lines: 12pt line=288 18.72 (18.48 once) for Cambria / Calibri / Times New Roman / Arial / Garamond / Aptos / Verdana / Century + MS Gothic or MS Mincho and for MS Gothic alone; 10.5pt single 13.68 (13.44 once); 12pt single 15.60 (15.36 once); MS PGothic the same

cases.note: Cambria + MS Gothic 12pt line=288: the EA factor, not Cambria's 1.172 and no Chromium union
two declared faces: the metric strut face leads the strut and the EA spans (a FontFace registered at layout time names itself in --doc-strut-face; jsdom has no FontFace)
Times New Roman + MS Mincho 10.5pt single
MS Gothic on both slots: a single face has no union to tame
